scope: Full lean stock xv6 forktest with the current opt-in protected32 native dispatcher; no emulator code change or speed claim

host.cpu: Intel Xeon Processor (Skylake, IBRS, no TSX), KVM, 4 vCPU
host.loadNote: The shared VPS had substantial competing load (10.78 one-minute load average on four vCPUs shortly after measurement). Wall times differ materially; the two user-CPU times are diagnostic, not a paired A/B.

workload.name: stock xv6-public forktest, 4 MiB, Bochs BIOS
workload.baselineCommand: XV6_LEAN=1 XV6_RAM_HASH=1 XV6_NATIVE_DISPATCH=1 XV6_FIRMWARE=bochs XV6_STEPS=40000000 XV6_STOP_ON_EXPECT=1 XV6_COMMAND=$'forktest\r' XV6_EXPECT_SERIAL=$'fork test OK\n$ ' node scripts/probe-xv6-stock.mjs
workload.profileCommand: XV6_LEAN=1 XV6_RAM_HASH=1 XV6_NATIVE_DISPATCH=1 XV6_FIRMWARE=bochs XV6_STEPS=40000000 XV6_STOP_ON_EXPECT=1 XV6_COMMAND=$'forktest\r' XV6_EXPECT_SERIAL=$'fork test OK\n$ ' node --cpu-prof --cpu-prof-dir=/tmp/bw386-shortspan-20260928 scripts/probe-xv6-stock.mjs
workload.summarizeNote: Use an empty profile directory so the glob expands to exactly one file.

categoryDefinitions.dispatcherMixed: all self samples in i80386-native-dispatch.js, chiefly run()
categoryDefinitions.directWindowValidation: all self samples in i80386-read-window.js and i80386-write-window.js, including prevalidation and validity checks
categoryDefinitions.nativeDecode: decode() and decodeI80386NativeByteBlock() self samples in i80386-native-byte-block.js
categoryDefinitions.cpuStateCopy: setCpuState() and copyStateToCpu() self samples in i80386-block-spike.js
categoryDefinitions.ordinaryCpuCore: all self samples in i80386.js, including ordinary fallback step and translation
categoryDefinitions.boardAndDevices: all self samples in i80386-at-machine.js, i8086-machine.js and named AT device modules
categoryDefinitions.otherHostRuntime: all remaining source positions, including probe, V8 GC and Node runtime

parity.comparison: Byte-for-byte identical complete JSON reports, including guest serial ending fork test OK, CPU/device state, native statistics and final physical RAM hash.

interpretation: V8 CPU-profile self samples provide source-position attribution, not exclusive phase timing. The 1,428 dispatcher and 2,158 native-runner samples are a mixed attribution envelope, not removable overhead: these frames include inlined cache lookup, block/code/window validation, event guards, CPU state transfers, and fallback decisions. Direct block-validation (25), window-helper (218), and state-copy (55) bins are lower bounds for their functions because V8 inlines work into callers; the window-helper bin includes prevalidation as well as validity checks. Ordinary CPU and board bins are attributed self samples from fallback execution, not a complete inclusive fallback cost. The raw profile is intentionally excluded from the PR; its hash and the media-free summarizer make the analysis reproducible.

prototypeGate.candidate: A bounded cheap-entry fast path for already decoded short protected32 native blocks, preserving code/window validity, event and fault boundaries, and all guest state. No opcode or grammar expansion in this milestone.
prototypeGate.planningCeiling: The 26.89% mixed-frame share is an attribution envelope, not entirely removable overhead. A prototype would need to eliminate at least 25% of those samples without shifting equivalent cost into other frames to plausibly clear a 5% end-to-end target. This is an untested hypothesis, not observed gain.
prototypeGate.retention: Predeclare at least 5% lower mean unprofiled user-CPU time over three serial paired baseline/candidate full xv6 runs, with all three pair directions favorable; byte-identical guest report and RAM hash for every run; focused event, fault, code-write, and page-window regression tests. If the gate fails, discard executable optimization and publish a negative receipt.
